findings.summary: Ten immutable P5 .2 task templates expose 15 lifecycle predicates that are not guaranteed by their reservation groups.

resolutions.priorSummary: P5 declares four external activation gates and remains review-only.
resolutions.evidence: The exact adapter and lifecycle primitives exist, while required receipts and external activation acceptance remain explicit gates.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: No live activation is allowed from this review-only report.

resolutions.priorSummary: P3/P6/P7 authoring dependencies are validated review inputs, not runtime-eligible production catalogs.
resolutions.evidence: The join uses immutable operational .4 provenance and does not promote P3/P6/P7 authoring to runtime authority.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: A later authorized activation slice is still required.

resolutions.priorSummary: The scheduler has no command surface that atomically activates/deactivates authored potential resources from ownership, hire, delivery, training, readiness, maintenance, stock and shift evidence.
resolutions.evidence: The versioned lifecycle primitive implements the exact 13 authored commands and atomic scheduler reprojection.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: The primitive is not embedded into the live save schema.

resolutions.priorSummary: Four locked P5 rooms requiring P6 ownership have no exact P6 assetCatalogId mapping.
resolutions.evidence: All 12 rooms participate in the exact 49-resource P5/P6 crosswalk with explicit asset IDs.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: Review-only crosswalk authority is not live activation authority.

resolutions.priorSummary: Five starting rooms have no P5 activation requirements, but P6 is the ownership authority and provides neither exact asset mappings nor a new-campaign ownership seed/exception; the cross-system activatable set is unresolved.
resolutions.evidence: Five authored starting rooms are explicitly owned, delivered and ready in lifecycle evidence.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: Renderer state is not ownership evidence.

resolutions.priorSummary: The two starting devices still require maintenance/stock evidence, while all 27 equipment stock gates lack an exact P6 inventory policy mapping.
resolutions.evidence: Otoscope and microscope have explicit starting evidence; 10 inventory categories and exact per-task consumption are joined atomically.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: No live economy/save migration is authorized.

resolutions.priorSummary: P5 authors imaging_staff, but P6 has no wage row for that role.
resolutions.evidence: The exact crosswalk supplies economic records for all 10 staff resources, including imaging staff.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: Product-owner staffing balance acceptance remains external.

resolutions.priorSummary: visit.checkin can only reserve the inactive administrator and has no authored doctor fallback.
resolutions.evidence: The adapter correctly keeps the administrator unavailable until an explicit hire and shift command; it does not invent a doctor fallback.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: Day-one production staffing flow requires product-owner acceptance before activation.

resolutions.priorSummary: Generated anyOf lists contain potential inactive resources; importing startsActive resources without an explicit filter leaves empty requirement groups and unknown resource IDs.
resolutions.evidence: All 49 exact resources are projected and inactive alternatives remain known but unavailable instead of being string-filtered or dropped.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: Availability is lifecycle authority, never renderer inference.

resolutions.priorSummary: Thirty-three research tasks create separate skill groups; five multi-skill tasks can reserve extra staff even when the base staff already owns part of the qualification, conflicting with capacity=1 and the single-qualified-staff rule.
resolutions.evidence: P5 .2 requirement groups are preserved as independent AND groups; the adapter neither merges them nor infers a single-worker shortcut.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: Any staffing balance change must be authored, not inferred by the adapter.

resolutions.priorSummary: All 11 research safe-route capabilities require the inactive administrator for referral coordination and have no doctor fallback on day one.
resolutions.evidence: Unavailable exact tasks return their authored safe route without requiring an invented local referral-coordinator reservation.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: A local staffing fallback is not invented.

resolutions.priorSummary: The runtime exposes the safe atomic handoff primitive but does not enforce P5 not_allowed/midpoint/urgent-quarter policy IDs.
resolutions.evidence: The adapter enforces not_allowed, midpoint and urgent-quarter policies before atomic reservation reassignment.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: Only active tasks at exact authored breakpoints may hand off.

resolutions.priorSummary: None of 447 capability mappings, including all 367 task-bearing capability configurations, declares a handoff policy; independent capability tasks cannot safely infer one.
resolutions.evidence: Handoff policy is resolved from the exact visit/research/usage task template rather than inferred from a capability token.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: Capability-only policy inference remains forbidden.

resolutions.priorSummary: Authored fractional handoff breakpoints have no minute-rounding rule, so the adapter cannot choose a deterministic valid minute without new policy.
resolutions.evidence: Fractional authored breakpoints are rejected; the adapter never rounds them to a campaign minute.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: An author-supplied rounding rule is required to enable those handoffs.

resolutions.priorSummary: Research tasks declare 11 route IDs while urgent-overcapacity declares generic safe_referral; runtimeOverrides carry no route ID and precedence is unspecified.
resolutions.evidence: The exact task safeRouteId is preserved and returned on unavailability; no generic route replaces an authored route.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: Unknown or missing route authority fails closed.

resolutions.priorSummary: Twelve null P3 fallbacks are defaulted to safe_referral, and 27 of 135 external-coordination tasks retain local physical requirements without an explicit local-versus-external branch contract.
resolutions.evidence: The adapter does not choose between local and external execution without exact authored reservation authority and returns the exact safe route when blocked.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: No automatic local-versus-external policy is introduced.

resolutions.priorSummary: urgentOvercapacity names explicit_stabilization_task but does not map it to an authored visit task template.
resolutions.evidence: When no exact stabilization task can reserve, urgent work remains blocked and exposes safe_referral instead of inventing a stabilization mapping.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: An explicit stabilization mapping is still required for that optional branch.

resolutions.priorSummary: All 21 used consumable capabilities map to P6 inventory policies, but there are no starting lots, no atomic scheduler/economy transaction, and no exact queued/in-flight stock ownership-transfer contract.
resolutions.evidence: Exact inventory reservations and lifecycle consumption commit with scheduler activation or do not mutate state; reload rejects half-applied ledgers.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: The live economy/save schema remains unchanged.

resolutions.priorSummary: cgm_sensor is authored as a reusable P5 equipment resource and P6 asset despite canonical consumable_device semantics; no approved migration rule exists.
resolutions.evidence: The adapter follows the immutable .2 resource and lifecycle declarations for cgm_sensor and performs no automatic device/consumable migration.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: Any semantic migration requires a new author source and activation review.

resolutions.priorSummary: P5 clock and queue policies are data only; no runtime driver advances campaign minutes and schedules queued work against them.
resolutions.evidence: Queue scheduling is driven only by explicit command minutes inside a persisted horizon; no automatic policy is invented.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: The existing live browser clock is intentionally not replaced or rewired.

resolutions.priorSummary: The 30-day staffing catalog is recommendation-only and no hire/shift/absence bridge binds player choice and P6 wages to scheduler availability.
resolutions.evidence: Hire, shift assignment/update/removal and explicit absence projection are persisted and reloaded atomically.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: Recommended staffing remains recommendation-only until player commands exist in an authorized runtime slice.

resolutions.priorSummary: P5 supplies fatigue bands and per-staff baseFatigue values (10, 6 and 0), but all 10 authored baseFatigue values are dropped from the generated resource projection and no explicit contract defines whether or how they seed runtime fatigue. Accumulation/recovery, delegation, absence, maintenance, urgent-overcapacity, activation and the transition from the two legacy doctors also remain unwired.
resolutions.evidence: Exact fatigue bands, activation, maintenance, absence, delegation limits and urgent fallback are validated in the review adapter.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: Fatigue accumulation/recovery balance and live legacy transition remain outside this review-only slice.

resolutions.priorSummary: P5 execution durations and P6 economy durations differ for 312 capabilities; the adapter needs an explicit two-clock authority rule and must not merge them automatically.
resolutions.evidence: P5 authoredDurationMinutes drives reservation time while P6 economic durations remain separate economic metadata and are never merged.
resolutions.remainingBoundary: Changing either clock requires its own author authority.
